transcription.tex: In this chapter you will integrate a greater variety of expressions and solve differential equations.
\textbf{Standard results}\par Know the antiderivatives of standard functions.\[\int\sec^2x\,dx=\tan x+C.\]

\textbf{Substitution}\par Introduce a new variable to make an integral easier.\[\int x\sqrt{2x+5}\,dx\]\[u=2x+5,\quad x=\frac{u-5}{2},\quad dx=\frac12\,du.\]\[\int x\sqrt{2x+5}\,dx=\frac14\int(u-5)\sqrt{u}\,du.\]
\textbf{Reverse chain rule}\par Think about what differentiates to give the expression.\[\int\cos4x\,dx=\frac14\sin4x+C.\]\[\int\sin^3x\cos x\,dx=\frac14\sin^4x+C.\]

\textbf{Integration by parts}\par Integrate a product using the product rule in reverse.\[\int x\cos x\,dx\]\[u=x,\quad \frac{dv}{dx}=\cos x,\quad \frac{du}{dx}=1,\quad v=\sin x.\]\[\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x-\int\sin x\,dx\]\[=x\sin x+\cos x+C.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: \textbf{Integrating partial fractions}\par Split a rational expression into partial fractions so that each term is easier to integrate.\[\int\frac{3x+5}{(x+1)(x+2)}\,dx\]

\textbf{Solving differential equations}\par Find one variable in terms of another without derivatives remaining. For \(V>0\):\[\frac{dV}{dt}=-kV\]\[\int\frac1V\,dV=\int-k\,dt\]\[\ln V=-kt+C\]\[V=e^{-kt+C}=Ae^{-kt}.\]
\textbf{Approximating areas: the trapezium rule}\par Instead of integrating, split the area under the graph into trapeziums and add their areas to approximate the total.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Challenge}\par Given \(\int_5^{11}\frac1{ax+b}\,dx=\frac1a\ln(41/17)\), where \(a,b\) are integers and \(0<a<10\), find two different pairs of values of \(a,b\).

An antiderivative is \(\frac1a\ln|ax+b|+\frac1a\ln k\), where \(k>0\) is a constant.\[\left[\frac1a\ln(k|ax+b|)\right]_5^{11}\]\[=\frac1a[\ln(k|11a+b|)-\ln(k|5a+b|)].\]The constant cancels, giving\[\ln\left|\frac{11a+b}{5a+b}\right|=\ln\frac{41}{17}.\]\[\frac{11a+b}{5a+b}=\pm\frac{41}{17}.\]

\textbf{Case 1}\par \(\frac{11a+b}{5a+b}=\frac{41}{17}\).\[187a+17b=205a+41b\]\[18a=-24b\quad\Rightarrow\quad3a=-4b.\]Thus \(a\) is a multiple of 4 between 0 and 10:\[a=4\Rightarrow b=-3;\qquad a=8\Rightarrow b=-6.\]

\textbf{Case 2}\par \(\frac{11a+b}{5a+b}=-\frac{41}{17}\).\[187a+17b=-205a-41b\]\[392a=-58b\quad\Rightarrow\quad b=-\frac{196}{29}a.\]This is not an integer for \(a=1,\ldots,9\). It would also put a pole inside the interval, so cannot define the given integral.\par The only pairs are \((4,-3)\) and \((8,-6)\); their denominators stay positive on \([5,11]\).

transcription.tex: How can we find \(\int x\cos x\,dx\)?\par Just as the product rule differentiates a product of two expressions, integration by parts can often integrate a product.\par \textbf{Integration by parts}\[\int u\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx=uv-\int v\frac{du}{dx}\,dx.\]

The product rule gives\[\frac{d}{dx}(uv)=v\frac{du}{dx}+u\frac{dv}{dx}.\]Both terms on the right are products. We can let \(u\frac{dv}{dx}\) represent a product such as \(x\cos x\).\par Rearranging:\[u\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}(uv)-v\frac{du}{dx}.\]Integrating both sides with respect to \(x\) gives the formula above.

transcription.tex: A cylindrical tank has diameter 20 m. Water flows out at a rate proportional to the cube root of its volume \(V\). Time \(t\) is in minutes and depth \(h\) is in metres.\par a. Show that \(dh/dt=-k\sqrt[3]h\).\par b. Find a general solution \(h=(P-Qt)^{3/2}\).\par Initially \(h=27\); after 10 minutes, \(h=8\).\par c. Find \(P,Q\).\par d. Find the time when \(h=1\).

\[V=\pi r^2h=100\pi h,\qquad\frac{dV}{dh}=100\pi.\]\[\frac{dV}{dt}=-c\sqrt[3]V=-c\sqrt[3]{100\pi h}.\]Outflow gives a negative rate. Using connected rates:\[\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{dh}{dV}\frac{dV}{dt}=-\frac{c\sqrt[3]{100\pi}}{100\pi}\sqrt[3]h=-k\sqrt[3]h.\]Recall the chain rule from Chapter 9.

\[h^{-1/3}\frac{dh}{dt}=-k\quad\Rightarrow\quad\int h^{-1/3}\,dh=\int-k\,dt.\]\[\frac32h^{2/3}=-kt+C\quad\Rightarrow\quad h^{2/3}=-\frac23kt+\frac23C.\]\[h=\left(\frac23C-\frac23kt\right)^{3/2}=(P-Qt)^{3/2}.\]Use this until the tank becomes empty.

transcription.tex: 1. A rabbit population \(P\) satisfies \(dP/dt=kP\), with \(k>0\) and time \(t\) in years. Initially there are 200 rabbits.\par a. Find \(P\) in terms of \(k,t\).\par b. For \(k=3\), find when the population reaches 4000.\par c. Explain a limitation of the model for large \(t\).
